1. Communication PrincipleLink

Every external document sent by UNYRA should feel like it came from a disciplined institution, not from an improvised back-office workflow.

The standard is defined by these required signals.

Communication standardRequired signal
ControlThe message shows that UNYRA knows the governing record, gate, owner, and next action.
ClarityThe recipient can understand the purpose, action requested, deadline, and linked matter without guessing.
AccountabilityThe sender, owner, and expected response path are explicit.
Premium brand disciplineThe communication uses approved institutional tone, structure, and brand closure.
Confidence in executionThe message reads as decision-ready, not improvised or reactive.

2. Mandatory Institutional MinimumLink

Every formal customer or supplier communication should clearly show the following minimum fields.

FieldRequired use
UNYRA brand mastheadIdentifies the communication as institution-grade UNYRA output.
Document or communication reference numberGives the release a controlled identifier.
Issue dateConfirms the timing of the outward position.
Sender name and roleShows who owns the message.
Recipient name and companyConfirms the counterparty and intended audience.
Subject or purposeStates why the communication exists.
Linked deal, shipment, or control referenceConnects the message to the accountable record when relevant.
Exact action requiredMakes the recipient's next move explicit.
Response deadlineDefines timing when response behavior matters.

Do not send important counterparty communication without those basic fields.

3. Template Use RuleLink

Use the following approved templates by default.

TemplateUse
01_templates/11_external-communications/Official-Document-Transmittal-MASTER.mdUse when sending a controlled document packet outward.
01_templates/11_external-communications/Institutional-Trade-Correspondence-MASTER.mdUse for formal one-message communication, notices, clarifications, or institution-grade letters.
01_templates/11_external-communications/Counterparty-Document-Packet-Index-MASTER.mdUse when the release contains multiple controlled files and the recipient needs one clear register.
01_templates/11_external-communications/External-Communication-Release-Checklist-MASTER.mdComplete before external release so UNYRA does not send informal, incomplete, or inconsistent packets.
01_templates/11_external-communications/Counterparty-Communication-Control-Register-MASTER.mdUse when management needs one board or register for active outward communication, open response deadlines, and escalation discipline.
01_templates/11_external-communications/Counterparty-Message-Framework-MASTER.mdUse when UNYRA needs one controlled drafting sheet so subject lines, openings, requests, deadlines, and escalation language stay institution-grade.

4. When To Use Which FormatLink

One formal message, request, or noticeLink

Use institutional trade correspondence.

Standard examples are listed below.

Example useFormat
Request for confirmationInstitutional trade correspondence.
Controlled clarificationInstitutional trade correspondence.
Delivery or release noticeInstitutional trade correspondence.
Document deficiency noticeInstitutional trade correspondence.
Deadline reminderInstitutional trade correspondence.
Formal acknowledgmentInstitutional trade correspondence.

One packet with multiple filesLink

Use all of the following packet controls together.

Packet componentRequired role
Official document transmittalIdentifies the release and the controlled packet being sent.
Packet indexLists every enclosed controlled file and revision.
Release checklistConfirms the packet is ready to leave UNYRA.

If the packet touches a contained payment, release, shipment, or handoff posture, complete the movement-posture, stop-rule, next-safe-movement, and revalidation fields in those documents before sending.

Sensitive or high-stakes releaseLink

If the release affects price, payment, delivery timing, claims position, compliance posture, or legal exposure:

Release controlRequired behavior
Checklist firstComplete the release checklist before the message leaves UNYRA.
Linked recordLink the communication to the correct deal, shipment, compliance, or founder-decision record.
Version controlConfirm the outgoing files are the latest controlled versions.
Containment alignmentIf the underlying movement is in containment mode, confirm the outward wording matches the executable-check board, scenario response review, executive risk register, and the live gate before sending.

5. Tone StandardLink

Counterparty communication should carry the following tone attributes.

Tone attributeRequired expression
FormalUses business-grade language suitable for banks, customs teams, procurement offices, and executive inboxes.
ConciseStates the matter, request, deadline, and owner without unnecessary narrative.
ExplicitMakes the required action and consequence of delay clear.
RespectfulKeeps the wording disciplined even when the counterparty is late, incomplete, or difficult.
Commercially clearProtects price, payment, delivery, claim, compliance, and release posture from ambiguity.

Avoid the following patterns because they weaken control.

Pattern to avoidWhy it weakens control
Chat-style wordingMakes the communication feel informal and harder to archive as a controlled record.
Vague promisesCreates expectation risk without a committed gate, owner, or date.
Emotional languageWeakens institutional tone and can escalate tension unnecessarily.
SlangReduces premium credibility and creates forwarding risk.
Inconsistent capitalizationMakes the communication feel unreviewed.
Long unstructured paragraphsHides the request, deadline, and accountable record.

Write like UNYRA expects the message to be forwarded inside a bank, customs team, procurement office, or executive inbox.

Use 00_brand/02_guidelines/UNYRA-Institutional-Communication-Style-Guide.md as the language source of truth when drafting.

6. Packet DisciplineLink

When multiple files are sent, the packet should identify the following fields.

Packet discipline fieldRequired answer
EnclosuresExactly what is enclosed.
Revision controlThe revision of each controlled file.
Counterparty actionWhat action the recipient should take.
Response deadlineThe next required response date or time.
UNYRA ownerWho owns follow-through after release.
Movement postureThe current stop rule and next safe movement if the packet touches a constrained release or payment posture.
Hold or revalidation statusWhat remains on hold or under revalidation if the movement is not yet fully cleared.

Do not make the recipient guess which attachment matters most.

7. Naming Convention for Live External CommunicationLink

Use this pattern for live counterparty communication folders or files when practical.

COMM-YYYY-###_Counterparty_Subject

Naming examples are listed below.

ExamplePattern signal
COMM-2026-011_AtlanticFoods_Formal-Offer-PacketFormal customer offer packet.
COMM-2026-012_GoldenHarvest_Supplier-Release-NoticeSupplier release notice tied to a controlled outbound message.

8. Storage RuleLink

Store the working communication set in the live folder that owns the matter.

Matter typeStorage location
Commercial releaseActive deal folder.
Logistics or release communicationShipment folder.
Onboarding or account communicationCustomer folder.
Qualification or sourcing communicationSupplier folder.

Do not bury key external releases only in email.

The repository should retain the evidence of what UNYRA sent, why it was sent, and what response was expected.

9. Release Gate RuleLink

Before a formal release goes out, complete the following gate steps.

Gate stepRequired action
1Confirm the correct source documents are current.
2Complete the release checklist.
3Confirm the right template is being used.
4Confirm naming, references, and recipient details.
5Save the communication record back into the live folder after sending.

10. Signature and Brand RuleLink

Use approved UNYRA signatures and compositions only.

Do not create improvised email footer art, stretched logos, or alternate lockups.

Use the approved founder or business-development signature assets from 00_brand/01_assets/04_signatures/ when a visual signature block is needed.

11. Escalation RuleLink

If the outgoing communication commits UNYRA on any of the following areas, the communication should reference the linked internal control record before it is treated as final:

Commitment areaRequired control posture
PricingConfirm the commercial source record and approval path.
Payment timingConfirm the funding, payables, or collections control answer.
Shipment releaseConfirm the live shipment, release gate, and movement posture.
Compliance postureConfirm the compliance record and any review or release condition.
Claim remedyConfirm the claim, credit, recovery, or remedy control record.
Exception approvalConfirm the founder-decision or exception-approval record.

If the outward message could be read as widening a contained payment or release posture, it should also reference the current movement posture and must not imply broader clearance than the gate allows.

12. Communication Control RuleLink

When multiple formal communications are live at the same time, or when silence from a customer or supplier is becoming material:

Control actionRequired behavior
Open the control layerUse the counterparty communication control register or board.
Track the releaseRecord what was sent and when it was sent.
Track the responseRecord what response is due and by when.
Define escalationState the escalation trigger explicitly.
Assign ownershipAssign one internal owner for follow-through.

Do not let institution-grade outbound communication collapse into inbox memory.

13. Response SLA RuleLink

For important formal communication, define the response SLA before the message goes out.

For response-SLA discipline, define the following answers before release.

SLA decisionRequired answer
Receipt confirmationWhen receipt confirmation is expected.
Full responseWhen the full response is expected.
First reminderWhen the first reminder goes out.
Escalation triggerWhen silence becomes escalation.
Hold or revalidation triggerWhen a hold, revalidation, or founder escalation should occur.

Use 01_templates/11_external-communications/Counterparty-Response-SLA-and-Escalation-MASTER.md when the response window matters commercially or operationally.

14. Containment Communication RuleLink

When a customer, supplier, broker, or forwarder is being updated on a matter already in containment mode:

Containment stepRequired behavior
Open the control boardUse the communication control board before outward wording is finalized.
Reconfirm live answerConfirm the executable-check board, scenario response review, executive risk register, and linked funding or release gate still carry the same answer.
State only the current postureCommunicate only the current controlled posture, the required next counterparty action, and the next safe movement if one is allowed.
Avoid premature release languageDo not describe the matter as fully released, fully approved, or clear to proceed unless the live gate has actually moved to that posture.

Do not let outward wording outrun the internal control answer.

15. Strategic Trust Review RuleLink

When a customer or supplier is strategically important and response behavior itself starts affecting release confidence, cash timing, account posture, or sourcing confidence:

Trust-review actionRequired behavior
Open the strategic reviewUse 06_dashboard/38_counterparty-trust/Strategic-Counterparty-Trust-and-Response-Review.md.
Judge behavior qualityReview acknowledgment quality, escalation frequency, and repeat response friction over time.
Decide relationship postureDecide whether UNYRA should keep scaling the relationship, tighten release posture, or build more fallback protection.
Carry the conclusionMove any material conclusion into the customer account review, supplier performance review, monthly strategic review, KPI scorecard, and executive risk register.

Do not treat repeated silence on important matters as only an inbox problem. Treat it as relationship-quality evidence.

16. Trust Tier and Release Posture RuleLink

When the strategic trust review shows that relationship behavior should change how UNYRA releases, grows, sources, or escalates:

Posture actionRequired behavior
Open the matrixUse 06_dashboard/39_trust-posture/Counterparty-Trust-Tier-and-Release-Posture-Matrix.md.
Assign trust tierSet an explicit trust tier instead of using only descriptive watch language.
Define operating postureDefine the matching release posture, growth pace, or sourcing fallback rule.
Refresh linked controlsUpdate any linked credit, release, capital allocation, or supply resilience control that should carry the posture.
Carry material impactMove material conclusions into the founder dashboard, monthly review, and quarter planning.

Do not leave a strategic counterparty on "watch" without saying what that watch changes operationally.
